newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court denies Jehovah's Witnesses status.
newsitem.headline: German court denies Jehovah's Witnesses status.

text.p: A German court ruled on Thursday that the Church of the Jehovah's Witnesses would not be granted the status of a public body because it forbade its members from taking part in political elections.

Public body status would have allowed the U.S.-founded Christian sect to benefit from centrally-collected tax revenues, to conduct prison visits and to demand representation on the advisory panels of broadcasters.

The Federal Administrative Court in Berlin ruled that the church's refusal to acknowledge public elections meant it could not be viewed as showing sufficient support for the German state for it to receive full recognition under public law.

The court said that, by granting public status to the church, which has its headquarters in New York, it could have left the door open for organisations opposed to Germany's democratic system to receive similar acknowledgement.
Jehovah's Witnesses have been present in Germany for around 100 years and say they have more than 190,000 German members.
A lawyer for the church said the ruling ran the risk of endangering the religious freedom of minorities in Germany.

Germany, sensitive on constitutional issues after the Nazis swept aside legal controls to come to power in the 1930s, said earlier this month it was putting the U.S. Scientology Church under observation to assess whether it had an anti-democratic intent.
